cards.explanation: The answer is the devil and Satan. John says it right out loud: the dragon is "…that ancient serpent who is the devil and Satan…" (Revelation 20:2). That's one enemy wearing a whole drawer full of name tags. Whichever name you hear, John means the same one. The angel grabs him and doesn't ask which name he prefers.

The answer is into the Abyss, friends. The angel had the key to the Abyss, and John says he "…threw him into the Abyss, shut it, and sealed it over him…" (Revelation 20:3). Key, chain, shut, sealed. That angel did not leave one detail to chance.

The word is deceive. John says the angel sealed the Abyss over him "…so that he could not deceive the nations until the thousand years were complete." (Revelation 20:3). Deceiving the nations is what he can't do while he's sealed in there. Until the thousand years are complete, that's off the table.

The answer is False. The seal lasts until the thousand years are complete, and John says, "After that, he must be released for a brief period of time." (Revelation 20:3). The release comes up again in verse 7. So the dragon doesn't stay sealed in for good, friends.

The answer is Jesus. John sees the souls of those beheaded "…for their testimony of Jesus and for the word of God…" (Revelation 20:4). Their testimony was about Jesus, and it cost them. Jesus is named right there in the verse.

The answer is that they come to life and reign with Christ, friends. John says, "…they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years." (Revelation 20:4). That's for the beheaded souls and for those who refused the beast and its mark. I think that's a hopeful thing to read after such a heavy picture.

The word is resurrection, friends. After telling us the rest of the dead wait, John says, "This is the first resurrection." (Revelation 20:5). Coming to life and reigning with Christ is what he's calling it. He uses a plain, direct word.

The answer is True. John says of those who share in the first resurrection, "The second death has no power over them…" (Revelation 20:6). Then he adds that they "…will be priests of God and of Christ…" Blessed and holy, like he said.

The answer is priests of God and of Christ, bakers. John says, "…they will be priests of God and of Christ and will reign with Him for a thousand years." (Revelation 20:6). They serve and they reign, both at once. John writes both in the same breath.

The answer is to fight a battle, friends. Satan goes out to deceive the nations "…to assemble them for battle." (Revelation 20:8). Gog and Magog are the names John gives here. The deceiving comes first, and the battle is what he gathers them for.

The answer is that fire comes down from heaven and consumes them. John says, "But fire came down from heaven and consumed them." (Revelation 20:9). The army surrounds the camp and the beloved city, and then the fire falls. John doesn't describe any fighting before that.

The answer is False, and I think this is a heavy verse. John says the devil, the beast and the false prophet "…will be tormented day and night forever and ever." (Revelation 20:10). He doesn't put a thousand years on it. The thousand years belong to the binding and the reign.

The answer is earth and heaven, friends. John says, "Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them." (Revelation 20:11). There's the great white throne, and the One seated on it has that kind of presence. John gives the picture and moves on.

The word is deeds. John says, "…the dead were judged according to their deeds, as recorded in the books." (Revelation 20:12). The books are opened, and one of them is the Book of Life. Deeds is the word John uses, friends.

The answer is True. John says, "The sea gave up its dead, and Death and Hades gave up their dead…" (Revelation 20:13). The sea isn't the only place the dead come from. Death and Hades give up theirs too, and each one is judged according to his deeds.

The answer is True, friends. John writes, "Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death…" (Revelation 20:14). He gives the lake of fire that name himself. Remember, he said earlier the second death has no power over those who share in the first resurrection (Revelation 20:6).

The answer is anyone not written in the Book of Life, bakers. John writes, "…if anyone was found whose name was not written in the Book of Life, he was thrown into the lake of fire." (Revelation 20:15). Anyone whose name isn't found in that book is the one thrown in. I think it's a sobering way to end the passage.
